name: folk
tagline: A lightweight CRM for people who hate CRMs: contacts, pipelines, notes and follow-ups, with a browser extension that scrapes profiles into your database.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is not hard: contacts, tags, custom fields, pipeline stages, notes, reminders. An agent will give you a local CRM with kanban pipelines and a decent search box in one sitting, and for a solo operator tracking 300 relationships that is genuinely enough. The parts that hurt are the plumbing: the browser extension that pulls a LinkedIn profile into a record in one click, two-way Gmail and calendar sync so every thread and meeting lands on the right person automatically, and the enrichment that fills in company, role and socials from an email address. Those are each a weekend of OAuth scopes, scraping fragility and third-party API bills, and the enrichment one you cannot really build at all, you rent it. Build it if you want a private relationship log; keep paying if the value is that the CRM updates itself while you do nothing.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you import contacts, tag and enrich them by hand, drag them through pipeline stages, log interactions and get a daily list of people you said you would follow up with.
requirements: a CSV or vCard export of your existing contacts
optional: a Google Cloud project if you later want Gmail read access
whatYouLose: One-click capture from LinkedIn and other profile pages via the browser extension
Automatic email and calendar sync, so your DIY timeline is only as current as your typing
Contact enrichment: company, title, socials filled in from an email address
Shared pipelines, per-seat permissions and team activity, if you ever stop being a team of one
Mobile access and the general absence of rough edges
moatNotes: The extension plus mailbox sync is what keeps the database from rotting. Manual CRMs die in about six weeks.
whyPeopleStillPay: A CRM is worth exactly as much as its freshness, and freshness comes from ingestion you do not have to think about. folk sells the ingestion: the extension, the mailbox sync, the enrichment, plus a UI that does not feel like enterprise sales software. A self-built version starts equal on day one and loses ground every day you forget to log something. If your relationship count is small and your discipline is high, the DIY build holds. If not, you are paying for a system that keeps working when you stop.
notes: The schema is a Tuesday, the habit is the hard part.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal CRM called "rolodex". Single user, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/rolodex.db, migrations in ./db/migrations run on boot
- Server Actions for all mutations, no separate API layer
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, nothing else required

Data model:
- person: name, emails[], phones[], company, role, location, links[] (label + url), tags[], notes (markdown), createdAt, lastTouchedAt
- interaction: personId, date, kind (email | call | meeting | dm | other), summary
- pipeline: name; stage: pipelineId, name, order; deal: personId, pipelineId, stageId, title, value (nullable), nextStep, dueDate
- custom fields on person: key/value strings, user-definable, no schema migration needed

Features, in scope:
- Contact list with instant fuzzy search across name, company, tags, notes (SQLite FTS5)
- Person detail page: fields, notes editor, interaction timeline, deals they appear in
- Kanban board per pipeline, drag cards between stages, optimistic UI
- "Follow-ups" home page: deals with dueDate today or overdue, plus people with lastTouchedAi older than a chosen number of days (make the threshold a setting)
- CSV and vCard import with a column mapping step and dedupe by email
- Full CSV export of every table, one click
- Keyboard: / focuses search, n creates a person, j/k moves the list

Explicitly out of scope, do not stub it, do not fake it:
- Gmail, Outlook, calendar or LinkedIn integration of any kind
- contact enrichment from third-party APIs
- sending email (use mailto: links only)
- auth, multi-user, sharing, mobile app

Seed the database with 25 fake people across two pipelines so the UI is not empty. Put nothing in .env beyond an optional DB_PATH. Write a README with setup, the data model, and a blunt paragraph on what this does not do.
